title: Army Weekly Briefing
description: Army leadership, force design, modernization, contracts and the signal and network enterprise.
readFirst: Covers the close of AUSA and the week after. New: Hegseth's Oct. 14 autonomy panel, I Corps' description of the NGC2 rollout, and a Breaking Defense account of NGC2 on the 25th Infantry Division's existing radios. Both top Army posts are still acting. No new NETCOM release was found in this window.

items.headline: Hegseth closes AUSA on Autonomous Warfare Command; LaNeve says FASCOM is a three-star, corps-level effort
items.summary: On the last day of AUSA, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth sat with the service secretaries for a panel on Autonomous Warfare Command, the four-star command he directed on Sept. 30. Stars and Stripes reports the command is meant to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities and, by the memo signed at the time, needs legislation before an Oct. 1, 2027 establishment. Acting Chief of Staff Gen. Christopher LaNeve said FASCOM will be led by a three-star and will begin building autonomous systems at corps level. Protesters interrupted the panel.

items.headline: Telle's first public speech as acting secretary; both top Army posts remain unconfirmed
items.summary: Acting Secretary Adam Telle opened AUSA on Oct. 12, six weeks after he was named acting secretary following Dan Driscoll's resignation. He said the Army is moving off what he called compound self-interest and announced a first manufacturing rodeo in early 2027 to stress-test supply chains. Gen. Randy George was removed as chief of staff in April and has not been replaced. LaNeve, the vice chief, is acting chief. This is still the leadership picture after AUSA.

items.headline: LaNeve redesignates Futures and Concepts Command as FASCOM
items.summary: Army Public Affairs reported Oct. 13 that LaNeve selected U.S. Army Futures and Concepts Command for redesignation as Futures and Autonomous Systems Command. The command will be led by a three-star and will consolidate the Combat Capabilities Development Command, Medical Research and Development Command, 75th Innovation Command, Joint Modernization Command and the Transformation Decision Analysis Center. The move follows Telle's Oct. 1 autonomy memo. FASCOM is meant to support the new portfolio acquisition executive for autonomy.

items.headline: I Corps commander: NGC2 now has to work from Japan to Australia, not island to island
items.summary: Lt. Gen. Matt McFarlane told DefenseScoop at AUSA that I Corps has started a deliberate rollout of Next Generation Command and Control at corps headquarters and its enabling brigades. He contrasted division prototypes with corps command posts in Honshu and Brisbane, and called the Pacific problem the tyranny of distance and disruption. He said the corps is fielding capabilities validated at Project Convergence Capstone 6, not gear that failed in the desert heat, and that scaling depends on resources. Over the next six months he is focused on joint and allied interoperability across classification levels.

items.headline: Air says its Army NGC2 software deal can reach $200 million over five years
items.summary: GovCon Wire reported Oct. 13 that Air has a potential five-year, $200 million Department of War contract supporting the Army's NGC2 software delivery, with initial work centered on I Corps. Air said the deal continues its NGC2 work. The company's AI-native readiness platform is aimed at sustainment planning. This is the vendor's ceiling figure, separate from the roughly $93.6 million one-year application awards the Army announced earlier in the month to nine companies including Air.

items.headline: NGC2 on the 25th Infantry Division's existing radios was not seamless
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported from AUSA that the 25th Infantry Division's September attempt to run Anduril's Lattice on its existing communications, during Lightning Surge 5 in Hawaii, did not go cleanly. Brig. Gen. Shane Taylor, portfolio management executive for the command-and-control information network, called it growing pains. Lockheed Martin is the integrator for the 25th ID's portion. Anduril's program manager said the TSM radios were not the same waveform or configuration used with the 4th Infantry Division. Taylor said the 25th will keep some legacy equipment because not every unit will get a fresh fielding like the 4th ID. That architecture is what I Corps units will be baselined on this fiscal year.

items.headline: AFCEA TechNet Indo-Pacific: WWT is hosting an Army GEMSS session in Honolulu
items.summary: WWT's public-sector calendar lists an Oct. 26 session at the Hilton Hawaiian Village during AFCEA TechNet Indo-Pacific. The session covers Cisco software entitlements under the GEMSS 2.1 contract, WWT's Enterprise Agreement+ customer-success work, Cisco certification training, Cisco Advanced Services to the Army, and a demonstration of SPINNAKER, WWT's enterprise enablement platform.
